title: Advertising wagon battles with Punch Miller and Jack Carey
summary: Bands bucked wagon to wagon on street corners; Durand with Frankie Dusen ran Punch off the corner.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. And you know like the band, the jazz band would meet on Sundays on advertising and buck against one another. Yeah. So I'd pull up there by Pete Lacoste and he'd be trembling, you know. Thought I was going to buck against him. I wouldn't buck. I'd just wave, you know, and go by. And me and Rene never did buck. And then Buddy Petit, we never did buck together, you know. But Punch and all them other trumpet players, you know. Chris Kelly? Yeah. Chris Kelly. They stopped in the back there, that time they had mule wagons, you know, and horse and stuff. They'd back the tailgate to each one together like that and let's play. Sometimes we'd be there three and four hours, one play and the other play, you know. Just on one corner. Yeah, on one corner. We wouldn't have time to finish advertising, you know. So I'll never forget, we was on Gravia and I was somewhere back that we were playing. I was playing with Frankie Dusen then. And we was playing, you know, music like Sally Trombone and all that kind of stuff, you know. And old Jack Carey, they was playing all kinds of different numbers. And we would run them away, we would run them off that corner. See, they left. And when Punch got way down to the next corner line there, I said, watch her calling back. I said, you need to know it, because I don't know how to play no blues like him, you know. I start to play in the blues. Punch said, stop, stop, stop, turn around. Then he turned to the wagon around and come back up there and we pull off and laugh at him.
He wouldn't even stay there and fight it out.

No, no. We was putting some music on them, you know. Sally Trombone, Miss Trombone and all that kind of stuff. And old Frankie Dusen was laying right in it, you know. Willie Humphrey was playing with us then. We had a good band, Lil' Alec playing bass. I done forgot who was playing drum. Pretty good band then.
